title: Surface tension & capillarity
examples: What is the difference between cohesion and adhesion?
How does the material of the liquid affect the capillary rise?
Can surface tension be measured in the lab?

explain.say: Today we explore surface tension in liquids.

items: Surface tension is a force acting at the surface.
It is caused by the cohesive forces between liquid molecules.
These forces pull the surface inward, like a skin.

explain.say: The energy stored at the surface is called surface energy.

draw.text: Surface Energy: Work to increase area

explain.say: Capillary rise shows how liquids move in narrow tubes.

draw.text: Capillary Rise: Liquid in narrow tubes

explain.say: The angle of contact tells us how liquid meets solid.

draw.text: Angle of Contact: Liquid meets solid

explain.say: When liquid wets the solid, the angle of contact is small.
In everyday life, think about drinking through a straw.

faq.q: What is the difference between cohesion and adhesion?
faq.a: Cohesion is the attraction between like molecules, like water molecules sticking to each other. Adhesion is the attraction between different types of molecules, like water sticking to glass.
asks: What causes water to stick together?
Explain the difference between sticking to self and sticking to other things.

faq.q: Does the temperature affect surface tension?
faq.a: Yes, generally, as temperature increases, the surface tension of the liquid decreases. This is because the molecules have more energy.
asks: Will surface tension change if I heat the water?
How does heat affect liquid surface tension?

faq.q: Why does water climb up in a narrow tube?
faq.a: Water climbs due to capillary action, which is a result of adhesion between water and the tube walls being stronger than the cohesive forces within the water.
asks: What is the science behind plants drinking water?
Why does the water level rise in a narrow pipe?

faq.q: What does a contact angle of zero mean?
faq.a: A contact angle of zero means the liquid wets the surface perfectly, indicating very strong adhesion between the liquid and the solid material.
asks: What does it mean if the angle is zero?
If the angle is zero, what is happening between the liquid and solid?

faq.q: Can surface tension be overcome by soap?
faq.a: Yes, soap molecules are surfactants; they disrupt the cohesive forces between water molecules, thus lowering the surface tension.
asks: What chemical lowers the surface tension of water?

facts: Surface tension arises from the net inward pull on the surface molecules.
Capillary action depends on both cohesive and adhesive forces.
For water on clean glass, the angle of contact is typically small, showing wetting.
Adding soap or detergent lowers the surface tension of water.

quiz.say: If the cohesive forces in a liquid are much stronger than the adhesive forces, the liquid will:

options.show: Exhibit poor wetting and bead up.
options.say: Exhibit poor wetting and bead up.

options.show: Rise high in a narrow tube.
options.say: Rise high in a narrow tube.

options.show: Show a contact angle near zero.
options.say: Show a contact angle near zero.

quiz.why: Strong cohesion means the liquid molecules prefer sticking to each other rather than to a different surface.

wrong.1: This requires strong adhesion to pull the liquid up.
wrong.2: A small angle means the liquid wets the surface well, implying adhesion is strong.
wrong.3: Spreading requires the liquid to overcome its internal cohesive bonds.

quiz.say: Which scenario best demonstrates capillary action?

options.show: A drop of mercury forming a perfect sphere.
options.say: A drop of mercury forming a perfect sphere.

options.show: Water moving up inside a thin piece of paper towel.
options.say: Water moving up inside a thin piece of paper towel.

options.show: A large puddle spreading across the floor.
options.say: A large puddle spreading across the floor.

options.show: Oil floating on top of water.
options.say: Oil floating on top of water.

quiz.why: This movement is due to the liquid being pulled up by adhesion to the paper fibers.

wrong.0: This shows very high cohesion and minimal adhesion, resisting capillary action.
wrong.2: Spreading is governed by gravity and surface tension balance, not capillary action.
wrong.3: This demonstrates surface tension differences, not the capillary rise mechanism.

quiz.say: If a liquid has a contact angle close to 180 degrees on a solid, it suggests:

options.show: The liquid will wet the surface perfectly.
options.say: The liquid will wet the surface perfectly.

options.show: The liquid molecules are strongly repelled by the solid surface.
options.say: The liquid molecules are strongly repelled by the solid surface.

options.show: The liquid has very low surface tension.
options.say: The liquid has very low surface tension.

quiz.why: A large angle means the liquid prefers to maintain its surface shape rather than spreading onto the solid.

wrong.0: Perfect wetting corresponds to a contact angle near zero degrees.
wrong.2: Surface tension is an intrinsic property, not directly determined by the contact angle.
wrong.3: Polarity relates to molecular charge, not necessarily the repulsion from a specific solid.
